title: LTX render package manifest
description: episodes/<slug>/<EPID>/exports/ltx-render-package/render-manifest.json — written at 04g by tools/build_render_package.py, never by hand. Describes a package that the vidgen-dist app's Batch tab (C:\pycode\app-vidgen-dist) ingests directly: a master-prompt.txt of @@ s{n} blocks plus a stills/ folder matched by the scene number prefixing each filename stem.

source_manifest_sha256.description: Hash of _context/ltx-prompt-manifest.json, so a package can be proven to match the prompts it was built from.

negative_prompt_sha256.description: exports/ltx-render-package/negative-prompt.txt — the ONLY place suppression lives. A suppression clause in a positive prompt causes the artifact it names and is rejected upstream by LTXV-D010.

settings.description: Read from vidgen-dist's own app/config.py on 2026-10-29, not from its README, which still documents the retired LTX-2.3 relay app. Re-verify against source before changing.

duration_seconds.description: SECONDS, not frames — the graph derives 1 + floor(fps*duration/8)*8 internally, which is what satisfies LTX-2.5's num_frames%8==1 rule. Never hand-enter a frame count. Locked to 20 for every clip on both channels by owner decision 2026-10-29.

img_compression.description: LTXVPreprocess. Validated as the causal anti-invented-character lever on LTX-2.3 and carried into the 2.5 graph unchanged — still unconfirmed on 2.5, see research section 6.

clip.description: The internal clip id (SCnn), matching _context/ltx-prompt-manifest.json. The package's own lowercase form is carried by `marker` (@@ s{n}) and `still_file` (s{n}.png).

marker.description: The exact section marker written into master-prompt.txt. Must sit alone on its line.

still_file.description: The still keeps its SCnn clip-id name from renders/stills/ (no rename). The app binds a still to a prompt by the scene number PREFIXING the stem (SC07 -> @@ s7; a suffix such as _v2 is ignored; two files for one number make that scene ambiguous). A mispaired batch renders successfully anyway — which is why tools/build_render_package.py re-reads the package with the app's own rules and the owner still eyeballs the pairing at the 04g gate.

is_pilot.description: Pilot clips are human-watched at 04h before the full batch renders. Selection covers at minimum the opening clip, dense/multi-speaker dialogue, multi-character staging, a difficult prop interaction, and an environment/camera continuity pair.
